title: Liquorice “juice”
recipeQuote: The juice of it is also very good for the voice, for which purpose it is thickened and then placed beneath the tongue: it is good, too, for the chest and liver

evidence.citation: The Natural History of Pliny, Volume 4 (of 6): Books XVIII–XXIII
evidence.text: The same preparation that is known to us as Spanish liquorice or Spanish juice.

evidence.citation: The Complete Herbal (incl. The English Physician Enlarged, Family Dispensatory, Last Legacies)
evidence.text: Succus Glycyrrhizæ simplex. Or Juice of Liquorice simple.

evidence.citation: The Complete Herbal (incl. The English Physician Enlarged, Family Dispensatory, Last Legacies)
evidence.text: College.] Infuse Liquorice Roots cleansed and gently bruised, three days in Spring Water, so much that it may over-top the roots the breadth of three fingers, then boil it a little, and press it hard out, and boil the liquor with a gentle fire to its due thickness.

label: case study of an extraction correction; the hypothesis is worth re-testing, not a claim that liquorice works or is safe
